nodes.summary: Let $a_1, \dots, a_m$ and $b_1, \dots, b_n$ be rational numbers such that every sum $a_i + b_j$ is the square of a rational number, and let $t$ be an integer and $k$ a rational number such that $k^2 a_i - t$ is an integer for every $i$ and $k^2 b_j + t$ is an integer for every $j$. Then the integers $a_i' = k^2 a_i - t$ and $b_j' = k^2 b_j + t$ are such that every sum $a_i' + b_j'$ is the square of an integer.

nodes.summary: For all integers $p, q, r, s$, put $a_1 = 0$, $a_2 = 16pqrs$, $a_3 = (p+q+r+s)(p+q-r-s)(p-q+r-s)(p-q-r+s)$ and $b_1 = 4(pr - qs)^2$, $b_2 = 4(ps - qr)^2$, $b_3 = 4(pq - rs)^2$. Then $a_i + b_j$ is a perfect square for all $i, j \in \{1, 2, 3\}$.
nodes.title: Four-parameter triples with square pairwise sums, family (3.1)

nodes.summary: For all integers $p, q, r, s$, put $a_1 = -(p+q+r+s)(p+q-r-s)(p-q+r-s)(p-q-r+s)$, $a_2 = -(p-q+r+s)(p-q-r-s)(p+q+r-s)(p+q-r+s)$, $a_3 = 0$ and $b_1 = (p^2 - q^2 + r^2 - s^2)^2$, $b_2 = (p^2 - q^2 - r^2 + s^2)^2$, $b_3 = (p^2 + q^2 - r^2 - s^2)^2$. Then $a_i + b_j$ is a perfect square for all $i, j \in \{1, 2, 3\}$.
nodes.title: Four-parameter triples with square pairwise sums, family (3.2)

nodes.summary: For all integers $p, q, r, s$, put $a_1 = 4(ps - qr)^2$, $a_2 = 4(ps + qr)^2$, $a_3 = (p^2 - q^2 - r^2 + s^2)^2$ and $b_1 = 4(p^2 - q^2)(r^2 - s^2)$, $b_2 = 0$, $b_3 = 4(p^2 - r^2)(q^2 - s^2)$. Then $a_i + b_j$ is a perfect square for all $i, j \in \{1, 2, 3\}$.
nodes.title: Four-parameter triples with square pairwise sums, family (3.3)

nodes.summary: Let $e_{ij}$, $1 \le i, j \le 3$, be integers such that the matrix of squares $(e_{ij}^2)$ is semi-magic, that is, all its row sums and all its column sums are equal. Put $a_1 = e_{13}^2$, $a_2 = e_{31}^2$, $a_3 = e_{22}^2$ and $b_1 = 0$, $b_2 = e_{21}^2 - e_{13}^2$, $b_3 = e_{11}^2 - e_{22}^2$. Then $a_i + b_j$ is a perfect square for all $i, j \in \{1, 2, 3\}$.
nodes.title: Triples with square pairwise sums from a semi-magic square of squares

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with an addition and a multiplication, and let $(a_i)_{i \in I}$ and $(b_j)_{j \in J}$ be families in $\alpha$ indexed by arbitrary types $I$ and $J$. They have all pairwise sums square when, for every $i \in I$ and $j \in J$, the sum $a_i + b_j$ is a square in $\alpha$, that is, $a_i + b_j = c \cdot c$ for some $c \in \alpha$.
nodes.title: Families whose pairwise sums are squares

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
